smt-2019-geometry-tiebreaker-01.title: Complete to a triangle
smt-2019-geometry-tiebreaker-01.body:
Extend rays $DA$ and $CB$ to meet at $E$. Then $\angle EAB=\angle EBA=60^\circ$, so $\triangle ABE$ is equilateral with $EA=EB=3$. Thus $ED=4+3=7$ and $EC=2+3=5$, and $\angle E=60^\circ$. By the law of cosines, $CD^2=5^2+7^2-2\cdot5\cdot7\cos60^\circ=25+49-35=39$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{39}$**

smt-2019-geometry-tiebreaker-02.title: Angle chase
smt-2019-geometry-tiebreaker-02.body:
Let $D''$ be the image of $D'$ under the reflection in $AC$; it lies on $AB$. Reflections preserve angles, so $\angle D'AC=\angle CAD''=\angle CAB=:x$ with $\tan x=\frac{BC}{AB}=\frac68=\frac34$, and $\angle DAE=\angle EAD'=:y$. Going around from $AD$ to $AB$ we pass $AE$, $AD'$, $AC$, $AD''=AB$, so $2y+2x=90^\circ$ and $y=45^\circ-x$. Then $\tan y=\frac{1-\frac34}{1+\frac34}=\frac17$.

Place $A=(0,8)$, $B=(0,0)$, $C=(6,0)$, $D=(6,8)$. $E$ lies on the perpendicular bisector of $CD$, the line $y=4$. Line $AE$ makes angle $y$ below the horizontal ($AD$), so $\frac{8-4}{x_E}=\tan y=\frac17$ gives $x_E=28$ and $E=(28,4)$. Therefore $DE=\sqrt{(28-6)^2+(4-8)^2}=\sqrt{500}=10\sqrt5$.

**Answer: $10\sqrt5$**

smt-2019-geometry-tiebreaker-03.title: Coordinates
smt-2019-geometry-tiebreaker-03.body:
Put $B=(0,0)$, $A=(0,p)$, $C=(q,0)$. The hypotenuse $AC$ is a diameter of $\omega_1$, so $p^2+q^2=36$ and the center of $\omega_1$ is $O=\left(\frac q2,\frac p2\right)$. The circle $\omega_2$ is tangent to both legs and has radius $2$, so its center is $P=(2,2)$; it is internally tangent to $\omega_1$, so $OP=3-2=1$.

$\left(\frac q2-2\right)^2+\left(\frac p2-2\right)^2=1\iff\frac{p^2+q^2}{4}-2(p+q)+8=1\iff9-2(p+q)+8=1$, so $p+q=8$. Then $2pq=(p+q)^2-(p^2+q^2)=64-36=28$ and the area is $\frac{pq}{2}=7$.

**Answer: 7**
